steps.title: Import Vue and RTK Query dependencies
steps.instruction: Import Vue, createApi, fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query', and configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit' in your Vue component file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary dependencies. You'll need Vue for the component, and the RTK Query functions for API setup.
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and RTK Query dependencies here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for Vue and RTK Query are added to the file.
successCriteria: Vue, createApi, fetchBaseQuery, and configureStore are properly imported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported all the required dependencies for RTK Query in Vue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some dependencies, but check if you're missing any from the instruction.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports don't match what's needed. Make sure to import Vue, createApi, fetchBaseQuery, and configureStore as specified.

steps.title: Create an API service with RTK Query
steps.instruction: Create a postsApi using createApi from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react' with a base query and a getPosts endpoint.
steps.hint: Use createApi to define an API service. Provide a reducerPath, baseQuery, and endpoints object with a getPosts query.
steps.seedCode:
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react';

// Create a postsApi using createApi with a base query and a getPosts endpoint
steps.expectedOutcome: The postsApi service is defined with a reducerPath, baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery, and a getPosts query endpoint.
successCriteria: postsApi is created using createApi with a reducerPath, baseQuery, and a getPosts endpoint.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the postsApi service with RTK Query.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've included all required parts: reducerPath, baseQuery, and the getPosts endpoint.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for createApi. You need to define reducerPath, baseQuery, and endpoints with getPosts.

steps.title: Configure the Redux store with the API service
steps.instruction: Create a Redux store using configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and add the postsApi reducer and middleware to it.
steps.hint: You'll need to import configureStore and use the reducerPath and middleware from postsApi in the store configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Redux store is configured with postsApi's reducer and middleware properly integrated.
successCriteria: The store is created using configureStore with postsApi.reducer added under its reducerPath and postsApi.middleware concatenated to the default middleware.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the Redux store with the RTK Query API service.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the reducer and middleware from postsApi in the store configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store configuration is incomplete. Remember to add postsApi.reducer under its reducerPath and concatenate postsApi.middleware.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' with a template section containing a div and a script section that exports the component.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can create a component by defining a template and exporting it as default. Use the 'export default' syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'App' is created with a template containing a div element and a script section that exports the component.
successCriteria: The component is named 'App', has a template with a div, and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named 'App', has a template with a div, and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure is incomplete. Check that you've named it 'App', included a template with a div, and exported it as default.

steps.title: Initialize the store in the Vue component
steps.instruction: In your Vue component's setup function, import the configured store and return it to make it available to the template.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the store from where you configured it and return it from the setup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store is imported and made available in the Vue component's setup function.
successCriteria: The store is imported and returned from the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported and returned the store, making it available to your Vue component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you both import the store and return it from the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store needs to be imported and returned from the setup function. Check your import path and setup function return statement.

steps.title: Define the useGetPostsQuery hook
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, destructure the useGetPostsQuery hook from the postsApi.
steps.hint: The postsApi object should be imported and available. Use destructuring to extract the hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: destructuring a hook from an API object
const { useGetDataQuery } = dataApi;
steps.expectedOutcome: The useGetPostsQuery hook is destructured and ready to be used for fetching posts data.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is correctly destructured from postsApi inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully destructured the useGetPostsQuery hook, making it available for data fetching.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're destructuring useGetPostsQuery from the postsApi object inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook wasn't destructured correctly. Check that you're extracting useGetPostsQuery from the postsApi.

steps.title: Call the useGetPostsQuery hook in setup
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, call the useGetPostsQuery hook to initiate the data fetch.
steps.hint: Call the hook without any arguments to fetch the posts data.
steps.analogousExample:
// Calling a hook in Vue setup
const { data, isLoading } = useGetDataQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called in the setup function, which will trigger the data fetch when the component mounts.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called in the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useGetPostsQuery hook. This will initiate the data fetch when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the useGetPostsQuery hook inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useGetPostsQuery hook needs to be called inside the setup function to fetch the posts data.

steps.title: Destructure the query result
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, destructure data, isLoading, and error from the query result object returned by useGetPostsQuery.
steps.hint: Use object destructuring on the result object to extract the three properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Destructuring from an object
const { data, isLoading, error } = useGetPostsQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: The query result is destructured into individual variables for easy access in the component.
successCriteria: data, isLoading, and error are destructured from the query result object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully destructured the query result, making the data, loading, and error states accessible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're destructuring all three properties: data, isLoading, and error from the query result.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to destructure data, isLoading, and error from the query result object.

steps.instruction: In your component's template, add a conditional element that displays 'Loading...' when the isLoading value is true.
steps.hint: You can use a v-if directive on an element to conditionally render it based on the isLoading value.
steps.analogousExample: // Conditional rendering in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will show a loading indicator when data is being fetched.
successCriteria: The template contains an element with v-if="isLoading" that displays 'Loading...' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the loading state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using v-if with the isLoading value and displaying 'Loading...' text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading indicator isn't quite right. Check that you're using v-if with the isLoading value and showing 'Loading...' text.

steps.title: Add an error state display
steps.instruction: In the template, add a conditional element that displays the error message when the error state exists. Use v-if to conditionally render a paragraph showing the error message.
steps.hint: Use v-if="error" to conditionally render an element. Inside that element, display the error message using {{ error.message }} or {{ error }}.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: conditional error display in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a paragraph that conditionally displays the error message when an error occurs during the query.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with v-if="error" that displays the error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error state handling to display error messages when queries fail.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some error handling, but make sure you're using v-if="error" and displaying the error message properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error display isn't working correctly. Check that you're using v-if="error" and displaying the error message in the template.

steps.title: Display the fetched posts data
steps.instruction: In the template, add a list that maps through the posts data and displays each post's title.
steps.hint: Use v-for to iterate over the data array and render each item's title property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a list of items
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display a list of post titles when data is successfully fetched.
successCriteria: The template contains a list that iterates over the data array and renders each post's title.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the posts list to display the fetched data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some list structure, but make sure to iterate over the data array and display each post's title.
steps.feedbackWrong: The posts list is not correctly implemented. Check that you're using v-for to iterate over data and render the title property.

steps.title: Add a refetch button to demonstrate cache
steps.instruction: In the template section, add a button element with the text 'Refetch Posts' that calls the refetch function when clicked. The refetch function is available from the query result object.
steps.hint: You can access the refetch function from the query result object. In the button's click handler, call refetch().
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that triggers a refetch
<button @click="refetch">Refresh Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a button that triggers a data refetch when clicked, demonstrating RTK Query's cache behavior.
successCriteria: A button with the text 'Refetch Posts' is added to the template, and its click handler calls the refetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a refetch button. This demonstrates how RTK Query allows you to manually trigger data fetching while leveraging its built-in cache.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it calls the refetch function when clicked and has the correct text 'Refetch Posts'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Check that you've added a button element with @click="refetch" and the text 'Refetch Posts'.
